# Forecasting Results: LSTM vs Persistence

*Generated by `python main.py evaluate` on 2026-11-12 21:55. All numbers come from this run.*

## How the experiment was run

- Data: Kolkata, 2018-06-16 to 2020-07-01; train to 2019-09-30, validation to 2019-12-31, test after (see `reports/preprocessing_decisions.md`).
- Inputs: previous 14 days of AQI, PM2.5, PM10, NO, NO2, NOx, NH3, CO, SO2, O3, Benzene, Toluene, doy_sin, doy_cos.
- 4 LSTM variants x 5 random seeds (42, 43, 44, 45, 46). Variants: predict tomorrow's AQI directly (*level*) or predict the change from today (*change*); 2 layers x 64 units (*large*) or 1 layer x 32 units (*small*).
- The variant was chosen by **lowest mean validation MAE**; alert thresholds were tuned on **validation**. The test period was scored once, after those choices.
- Honesty note: test results of the very first model (level_large, seed 42) had already been seen before this experiment was designed. The design above was fixed before any of its own results were seen.

## 1. Validation results (used for selection)

| variant | target | size | MAE (mean ± sd over seeds) | RMSE | Bias |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| level_large | level | 2x64 | 41.5 ± 3.0 | 52.0 ± 3.3 | 13.7 ± 4.7 |
| level_small | level | 1x32 | 36.7 ± 3.1 | 46.0 ± 3.7 | 10.2 ± 6.0 |
| change_large | change | 2x64 | 32.5 ± 0.2 | 44.2 ± 0.1 | 3.4 ± 3.1 |
| change_small (selected) | change | 1x32 | 31.9 ± 0.5 | 43.7 ± 0.5 | 2.2 ± 2.4 |
| Persistence | - | - | 32.4 | 45.2 | -2.7 |

**Selected: change_small.**

## 2. Test results (scored once)

| forecast | MAE | RMSE | MAPE_% | R2 | Bias |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LSTM change_small: single runs (mean ± sd of 5) | 20.3 ± 1.0 | 30.1 ± 1.0 | 18.8 ± 1.7 | 0.846 ± 0.010 | 5.8 ± 1.6 |
| LSTM change_small: average of 5 runs | 19.8 | 29.6 | 18.2 | 0.851 | 5.8 |
| Persistence | 20.5 | 31.4 | 17.2 | 0.833 | 1.3 |

- Test MAE: LSTM (average of 5 runs) 19.8 vs persistence 20.5 - the LSTM is lower (better) by 0.7 AQI points.
- Difference in MAE (LSTM - persistence): -0.7, 95% block-bootstrap interval -1.9 to +0.5. The 95% interval includes 0, so on this test period the data **cannot distinguish** the LSTM from persistence.

Test MAE for every variant (shown for transparency only - **not** used to choose):

| variant | test MAE, average of 5 runs | test MAE, single runs | test Bias |
|---|---|---|---|
| level_large | 22.3 | 23.6 ± 4.7 | +15.8 |
| level_small | 20.1 | 21.0 ± 3.2 | +13.9 |
| change_large | 20.1 | 20.5 ± 0.9 | +5.5 |
| change_small (selected) | 19.8 | 20.3 ± 1.0 | +5.8 |

## How to read these results honestly

- The test period is 183 days from one half-year, including the COVID-19 lockdown (from 2020-03-25, external fact), when pollution patterns were unusual.
- The 95% interval accounts for day-to-day luck in the test days, not for how the model would do in other years.
- These are associations learned from past data; they do not show what *causes* pollution.
